mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the CPI growth exceeds 2% annualized, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to increased wage pressures and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over the past 3 months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS shows sustained growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past 3 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy in a tight labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy in tight labor market
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and UNRATE < 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% and retail sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 5% over the past 3 months, the combined signal indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 10% and RSAFS increases > 5% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increases by >10% and RSAFS by >5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months, the combined signal indicates a robust labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.5pp in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by >200k and UNRATE decreases by >0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% and an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% over the past 3 months signal a contractionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases > 1% and FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by >1% and FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.
